body:
WHAT
Streamed output — the model's reasoning (thinking_delta) and its answer (text_delta) — costs the renderer the same per delta however long the stream has already run.
- Reasoning deltas are held on their own reasoning block and written to the page at most once per animation frame (a short fallback timer covers a window that draws no frames). While the block is live, its body keeps only the latest ~8,000 characters, after one line that says how many earlier characters are held back. The whole reasoning is written into the block when the block ends (a tool call, the answer text, or the turn end). A restored session shows every reasoning block in full, as before.
- Answer text still reaches the page on every delta, because the streaming-Markdown contract is observable at once. What moves to once per frame is the check "was the user at the live edge?" and the scroll that follows it, so no delta forces a layout of the transcript.
- The now-line reads "thinking · 45s" / "responding · 12s". It never echoes a streamed token, and its timer runs from the start of the reasoning or answering stretch instead of restarting on every delta.
- Nothing is reordered. A block is finished (its buffered text written) before the tool row, answer or turn end that follows it. Each tab's text stays in its own block, so a background tab's reasoning never lands in the focused tab's transcript.

WHY
In the 2026-09-23 field test (docs/reports/2026-09-23-magentra-field-test, findings U-01, U-09, R-1) the window showed "reasoning" for 25 minutes while the engine was writing files, and then every step seemed to finish in 0 s. onThinkingDelta appended one text node per token (127,802 in that run) and read scrollHeight around each one. Measured on the real app through the real IPC channel, with the reasoning block open: 2,000 deltas took 6.7 s at the start and 109.9 s after 10,000 (the cost grows with the square of the length), and a task_list_updated sent after 12,000 deltas reached the task rail 301 s later. With the block closed the cost was linear (about 0.25 ms per delta) but the body still grew by one DOM node per delta. An answer that is one long block with no committable blank line showed the same quadratic shape (3.2 s to 28.7 s per 2,000 deltas). The now-line read "thinking · Enemy · 0s" because every token replaced its detail and restarted its timer.

WHERE
app/renderer/modules/landing.js — onThinkingDelta(text), onTextDelta(text), onSessionRestored() (reasoning replay). app/renderer/modules/stream.js — finalizeThinkingEl(), the reasoning block's buffer and its per-frame flush, commitStreamedMarkdown(el). app/renderer/modules/util.js — withAutoScroll() and the once-per-frame live-edge follow, scrollContainer(), isNearBottom(). app/renderer/modules/views.js — setNowActivity(), renderNowText(). Frames reach the page unchanged through app/main.js sendToRenderer("engine:event", {...frame, tabId}) → preload onEvent → routeEngineEvent (tabs.js).

TEST CHECKLIST (every frame is sent through win.webContents.send("engine:event", …) in the main process — never a direct call into the renderer)
1. 6,000 thinking_delta frames (seeded, about 4 characters each, like the field log) sent in one burst to an OPEN reasoning block: the median cost of a 500-delta slice in the last 2,000 is at most twice the median in the first 2,000 (a ratio, not milliseconds). While live, the block's body holds at most 3 DOM nodes and at most 12,000 characters. After a tool_call_started ends the block, its text is exactly every delta joined in order, and the tool row sits after it.
2. At the field run's peak rate (250 thinking deltas per second for 20 s) with the block open, a task_list_updated sent right after the stream is handled within a quarter of the stream's own duration, and the task rail shows the task.
3. During a paced reasoning stream the now-line never contains a streamed token, reads "thinking · <n>s", and n never goes down and ends above zero (deltas do not restart it).
4. An answer that is one long code block — 6,000 text_delta frames after an opening fence, with blank lines inside the fence (which must not commit) — sent in one burst: the median cost of a 500-delta slice in the last 2,000 is at most twice the median in the first 2,000. After the fence closes and the turn ends, the message renders as one code block holding exactly the text sent.
5. Two workspaces tiled, the second focused: reasoning deltas for the first tab appear only in the first tab's pane and the focused pane gains no reasoning. Moving focus to the first tab while its deltas are still arriving loses none of them: its block ends holding exactly the text sent, in order.
6. A session_restored whose message carries a 200,000-character reasoning block shows all 200,000 characters in that block.

ADDED 2026-09-24 (audit follow-up):
- (ui) A noisy command's live tail measures the live edge once per frame, not once per output delta (a pass-through count of scrollHeight reads: at most one per five deltas), and still ends at the last line sent.
